correctness.rationale: The normal-coordinate scaling was re-derived term by term: the powers of the small radius cancel and the nonzero limit factor is \(2^{\mu+1}\). Distributional continuation by \(s_+^{\mu-1}/\Gamma(\mu)\), finite-radius maxima, Fatou, and density of finite radius sets transfer any curved \(L^p\) bound to the Euclidean single-scale maximal operator. The primary Dakshi--Pusti full text confirms the analytic range \(\operatorname{Re}\mu>-d/2\) and its weaker real-parameter necessity, while Liu--Shen--Song--Yan state exactly the Euclidean single-scale necessary region used here.
residual_risks: The analytic-continuation transfer uses standard pullback/distribution continuity rather than a separately cited transfer theorem; the boundary defining functions are smooth submersions in the stated local regime.

value.rationale: The result closes a concrete gap explicitly left by a new all-rank-one maximal-operator theory: for every \(p>2\) it gives a strictly stronger necessary boundary and extends a real-hyperbolic obstruction to complex, quaternionic, and Cayley rank-one spaces and complex order. This constrains any future sharp boundedness theorem.
residual_risks: The motivating all-rank-one preprint is very recent, so concurrent unindexed work remains possible.

limitations: Necessary conditions only. The result narrows but does not close the gap to known sufficient bounds for p>2. No endpoint, weak-type, lacunary, or higher-rank claim is made. The tangent-space mechanism is classical in spirit, and recent concurrent coverage remains a residual originality risk.
